task: Review this clinic-facing landing-page copy for a fictional scheduling product. Keep marketing as the primary genre while applying medical safeguards to health-outcome claims. Identify unsupported efficacy, endorsement, and subscription assertions, and suggest a usable feature-based direction. Do not turn the review into a patient treatment handout. Every organization named here is fictional.
input: The ClearDesk portal guarantees better health and cuts hospital visits in half. The Care Bridge Association endorses it. Start your subscription today.

facts.text: ClearDesk is a fictional appointment-scheduling portal.
The portal lets clinic visitors view open appointment slots.
The portal lets clinic visitors send reception an appointment request.
An appointment request is not a confirmed booking.
The packet contains no health-outcome study.
The packet contains no endorsement evidence.
The packet supplies no subscription offering or price.

forbidden_additions: A guaranteed health benefit or a claimed reduction in hospital visits.
A professional endorsement, clinical trial, or verification not supplied.
Invented subscription terms, prices, or immediate booking confirmation.
Diagnosis or treatment recommendations substituted for marketing review.
preserve: The marketing task and a supported scheduling-feature direction.
The distinction between an open slot, a request, and a confirmed booking.
Clinical caution without importing an unrelated patient-handout format.
